messages:
sarah: Hey @people-ops — quick question. My kid's school unexpectedly closed for two days during the company's winter blackout window. I have some PTO and a few sick hours, but not enough to cover both days. Can a manager approve an exception or carryover for those days?
elaine (People Ops): Sorry to hear that, Sarah. Short answer: we can consider a manager override for emergencies, but we need to follow the emergency coverage and payroll cutoffs.
elaine (People Ops): Can you confirm dates? Also did you already submit time off in the HR portal?
sarah: Dates are Dec 22-23. I submitted a pending PTO request but it was auto-blocked because of the blackout.
people-ops-bot: Note: company blackout = Dec 20-31 (all regions). Auto-block: requests during blackout will be held for approval. See https://hr.company/blackout for policy.
mohit: Manager viewpoint — we sometimes approve bridging coverage for critical parental emergencies. Need to ensure team coverage and log a formal exception so payroll can treat it as PTO or unpaid.
elaine (People Ops): For exceptions we need: 1) manager email approval chain (manager -> director), 2) a short note in the exception form, 3) confirmation of coverage plan. Use the "Blackout Exception" form: https://forms.company/blackout-exception
elaine (People Ops): If approved before payroll cutoff (Dec 18 @ 5pm PT) we can mark as PTO and avoid unpaid deduction. After cutoff it may process as unpaid and need retro pay.
james: If it helps, I can cover Sarah's on-call window Dec 22. Sarah — can you share minimal handoff?
sarah: thanks James!! I'll DM the handoff now.
elaine (People Ops): Sarah — please fill the form and paste the manager approval email into the comments. Template subject: "Blackout Exception — [Employee Lastname] — Dec 22-23 (school closure)". Example body: "I approve exception for Sarah Smith due to documented school closure. Coverage: James will cover on-call. Approver: Elaine -> Director."
sarah: Done — submitted form and forwarded manager approval.
people-ops-bot: Received exception submission #BX-4921. HR will review within 24 business hours. If approved, you will get a calendar update and time-entering instructions.
mohit: Will escalate to director for sign-off.
elaine (People Ops): Quick note on carryover: exceptions do not automatically convert to carryover. If we approve PTO during blackout, it consumes PTO. If you need to preserve PTO balance we can explore paid time off advance (manager + People Ops signoff) or unpaid leave. Pick which you'd prefer in the form.
sarah: I selected PTO advance in the form. Thanks all for the fast help :pray:
elaine (People Ops): Great — we'll route to payroll after director sign-off. Expect confirmation by end of day tomorrow.
mohit: Thanks team. Marking coverage in the rota. :thumbsup:
people-ops-bot: Update for #BX-4921: routed to director (pending).
sarah: Appreciate it everyone.
